about: Neighbourhood benchmarks for the sponsor's question, how Greenmount compares on public asking retail rents and storefront vacancy (no CoStar or paid data). One object per neighbourhood: asking rents with the lease type as stated, vacancy with its definition, residents, displacement evidence and a rating under the case library's written rubric. Every value comes from a page read on the access date; the shared brief is in the team report.

neighbourhoods.why_comparable: Fair as a historic Black main street with theatres and nightlife; unfair on rents: a Metro stop and heavy redevelopment made it high-income (~$167k median HH), so it is a displacement cautionary case for Waverly.

neighbourhoods.rating_reason: Moderate: contract rents up ~64% (nominal) and a laundromat and furniture stores gone as one family bought 18+ buildings, but no source documents mass displacement; the 11.5% population fall is not tied to galleries.

context.storefronts_or_length: 8 galleries open and 2 opening (NYT, May 2024); 18 buildings within a three-block radius bought by one investor family since 2019 (ABC7)

neighbourhoods.why_comparable: Fair on scale and income: a small historic district, ~90% renters, median HH ~$54k. Unfair on drivers: majority Latino and Asian, and one investor family bought 18+ buildings to seed a gallery district.

displacement_evidence.value: Black share ~3/4 (2000) to ~1/2 (2015); median rent +77% 2005-15; 2015 median income $50,200 new vs $28,000 long-term residents; OSC: costs fed 'increased displacement'
displacement_evidence.source_title: NYS Comptroller (OSDC), An Economic Snapshot of the Bedford-Stuyvesant Neighborhood, Report 5-2018 (Sep 2017)

displacement_evidence.indicator: Black and white resident counts, Census 2010 vs 2020 (NTAs Bed-Stuy East and West)
displacement_evidence.value: Black residents down 22,000+ (East ~57,000 to 45,600; West ~41,300 to ~31,000); white up 30,000+ (share ~10% to 26%+); from majority-Black to under half
displacement_evidence.source_title: Patch (Bed-Stuy), Bed-Stuy lost 22K Black residents, gained 30K whites in decade (18 Aug 2021)

displacement_evidence.indicator: Long-standing business closed
displacement_evidence.value: Head Hunter Barbershop, 1092 Bedford Ave, closed Dec 2014 after nearly 70 years, citing 'an increase in rent and gentrification'; a Fulton St clothing store gave way to a national gym chain
displacement_evidence.source_title: DNAinfo New York, MAP: 7 Bed-Stuy Businesses That Shuttered in the Last Year (30 Jan 2015)

displacement_evidence.indicator: Retail rent escalation and pressure on small businesses (Fulton St)
displacement_evidence.value: Brokers sought ~$50/sq ft in 2015; $40-$90/sq ft by 2023, top end in new Fulton St buildings; article reports concern small local businesses could be pushed out
displacement_evidence.source_title: Commercial Observer, Developers Have Rediscovered Bedford-Stuyvesant. Can It Sustain the Boom? (30 Jan 2023)

neighbourhoods.rating_reason: OSC links rising housing costs to displacement as the Black share fell from ~3/4 to ~1/2 (2000-15); 22,000+ Black residents lost 2010-20; a 70-year barbershop closed citing rent and gentrification.

context.historic_district: Three major historic districts covering 1,600+ residential buildings, public buildings and churches (NYS Comptroller, 2017); brownstone fabric
context.anchor_institution: Restoration Plaza (Bedford Stuyvesant Restoration Corp.) on Fulton St; Interfaith Medical Center; Pratt Institute nearby (CDNA map)
context.transit: Six subway lines (A, C, G, J, Z, S) incl. Nostrand Ave, Kingston-Throop and Utica Ave stations; eight bus routes incl. B15, B25, B26, B38, B43, B44, B52 (CDNA)
context.storefronts_or_length: 879 storefronts on 6 CDNA corridors (Fulton St Classon-Troy: 369); Bed-Stuy Gateway BID on Fulton St covers 1.5 miles of corridor (OSC)

neighbourhoods.why_comparable: Fair on history, Black heritage, brownstone fabric and main-street strips with ~24% vacancy (2021); less fair on scale, density, transit and today's much higher incomes and home values.
